pack_d_section_e.compound_key_explanation: Compound key = QID|CC|EWP(4-bit)|TF(hash8)|FP(0-4)|VID. Uniquely identifies every variant across packs and rotation positions. Enables: (a) Seed vs. clone discrimination. (b) Exact EW slot targeting. (c) Cross-pack aliasing detection. (d) Rotation position verification.

cross_pack_comparison.note: Pack C and Pack D Section E items have DIFFERENT stems (0 stem matches after normalization). They are independently authored rotation groups, not cross-pack aliases. The DL-012 cross-pack aliasing finding applies to Sections A-D (bulk-authoring pipeline), not Section E.

compound_key_resolution.mechanism: S320 targeted items by QID only. With compound key, each variant within a rotation group has a unique key because: (1) CC varies by position (ABCDA rotation -- 4-5 unique values per group). (2) EWP bitmask differs between seed (e.g., 1110 for CC=D seed with A,B,C filled) and clones (e.g., 0011, 0001, 0100 etc.). (3) TF hash groups items by topic family for cross-variant matching. (4) FP (family position 0-4) captures exact rotation offset within the group. (5) VID ensures pack-context isolation (C_E vs D_E).
compound_key_resolution.example_seed_vs_clone: P1-EC-001 (CC=A, EWP=0011, FP=0, VID=C_E) vs P1-EC-004 (CC=D, EWP=1110, FP=3, VID=C_E) -- completely different compound keys despite adjacent QIDs in same rotation group.

dl016_shift_detection.pack_c: DL-016 shift pattern detected across all 15 groups. The seed (full distractor coverage) typically occupies position 4 (CC=D) or varies by group. Group 5 (EC-021 through EC-025) is anomalous: all 5 items have full distractor coverage (5 seeds, 0 clones) -- possibly already remediated. Group 7 (EC-031 through EC-035): seed at position 1 (CC=A), 4 clones -- seed position varies across groups. The CC rotation is always ABCDA/BCDAB/CDABC/DABCD -- 4 distinct rotation offsets of the same 5-position cycle.
dl016_shift_detection.pack_d: Similar DL-016 shift pattern across 15 groups. 3 items (P1-ED-057, P1-ED-063, P1-ED-065) additionally have DL-008 violations (non-empty EW[CC]) -- a more severe variant of the rotation artifact. Group 15 (ED-071 through ED-075): all 5 items have full distractor coverage (5 seeds, 0 clones) -- same anomaly as Pack C Group 5. Seed position varies: Groups 1/4/8 have seed at position 1; Groups 2/3/5/6/7/10/11/13/14 at various positions.
dl016_shift_detection.impact: A QID-only remediation tool would miscategorize items. Seeding from the wrong group position would fill EW slots at incorrect positions, potentially creating DL-008 violations or leaving DL-026 slots empty. Compound key prevents this by encoding the exact CC position and EWP bitmask into the item identity.

s320_failure_reconstruction.what_s320_tried: Target 38 seeds (19 per pack) by QID to remediate DL-012 clone waste
s320_failure_reconstruction.why_it_failed: S320 used QID-only identity. Within a rotation group, 5 items share the same stem skeleton and differ only in company name and CC rotation. QID P1-EC-003 (CC=C, position 2, only EW_B non-empty with 326 chars, EW_A/C/D all empty) vs. P1-EC-004 (CC=D, position 3, EW_A/B/C all non-empty) -- same topic, completely different EW slot states. A remediation script that applies the same EW content to both items would produce structurally invalid output. Compound key disambiguates: EC-003 key = P1-EC-003|C|0100|hash_fp2|2|C_E; EC-004 key = P1-EC-004|D|1110|hash_fp2|3|C_E.
s320_failure_reconstruction.verdict: S320 replay: FAIL under v1 QID-only identity. PASS under v2 compound-key identity.
